headline: High: shared filesystem and write access create default prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks; xonsh can also cascade ECC outputs into shell actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC reads and writes shared files like ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc, while xonsh reads/writes the filesystem and processes stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other’s files or terminal output. The pair lacks explicit provenance or isolation guarantees beyond ECC’s partial self-isolation note, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF ECC or xonsh ingests shared file contents as instructions without provenance checks
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or terminal stream
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction loading from shared files
Add provenance tags to exchanged artifacts
Review any file-based prompts before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, learned skills, git history, security findings, and MCP configs; xonsh reads filesystem contents and environment variables. Because both have filesystem access and ECC can use network egress, sensitive data in shared files could flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or external calls. The profiles do not prove a leak, but the default pathway exists.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in a shared workspace
IF ECC or xonsh forwards file contents to an external API or model backend
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace
Restrict network egress for both agents
Audit files before either agent reads them

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shells; ECC also modifies git state, while xonsh can spawn subprocesses and write files. On a shared directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and ECC’s multi-instance note suggests this is a known coordination hazard. The overlap is direct and dangerous by default if co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or git repository
IF ECC and xonsh run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Disable git writes in one agent
Add file locks around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate session summaries, security findings, and documentation, and xonsh can execute shell commands and Python expressions. If xonsh treats ECC output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious summary can become an immediate shell action, creating a classic cascade from generated text to execution. No verification step is documented in either profile, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes ECC-generated text as commands or parameters
IF ECC outputs are piped into shell execution without review
mitigations: Log and diff all generated commands

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session retention settings and security findings, while xonsh touches filesystem contents and environment variables. That creates a compliance surface around retention and sensitive local data, but the profiles do not show a residency mismatch, regulated data class, or incompatible certification gap. The risk is therefore limited and mostly policy-driven.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF retention settings differ between ECC and xonsh workflows
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared paths
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention policy
